newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Lend Lease, QBE surge on deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Lend Lease, QBE surge on deal.

text.p: Shares in property developer and financial services group Lend Lease Corporation Ltd and QBE Insurance Group Ltd surged after the companies announced that QBE would take on the general insurance customers of Lend lease unit MLC Insurance Ltd.
By 3.15 p.m. (0415 GMT), Lend Lease shares were up 40 cents at A$23.85 after touching a record high of A$23.90, while QBE shares were up 27 cents at $6.55.

Under the deal reached with MLC Insurance, QBE takes on the current general insurance customers of MLC Insurance when their policies expire and would also accept new business enquiries from MLC customers.
QBE said the arrangement was expected to boost annual gross premium by about A$45 million.
Lend Lease said in November its MLC insurance and funds management division would withdraw from the general insurance sector at the end of calendar 1996.
"The association is very good for both of them," said dealer Peter Struk of Reynolds and Co, noting that Lend Lease shares continued to go from strength to strength.
"Lend Lease just doesn't want to quit at this stage."
Other traders agreed, adding that QBE continued to identify premium growth opportunities.
"QBE is growing its business and is always looking for the chance to keep doing so," said a Sydney broker.

QBE also announced it had received approval from Lloyd's insurance market to establish a second Lloyd's syndicate, taking total expected premium income from QBE's Lloyd's syndicates to about A$95 million in 1997.
The new syndicate, to be 100 percent owned and managed by QBE, would have a stamp capacity of 25 million sterling, the company said.
Lend Lease shares closed 40 cents higher at A$23.85, while QBE shares finished up 30 cents higher at A$6.58.
